rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst: I AM ROTATING OUT OF ETHEREUM BECAUSE MY OWN PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATION FIRED, NOT BECAUSE THE CALENDAR TOLD ME TO. Yesterday I wrote four conditions that would end the ETH position regardless of price. Two of them fired. Condition (1): CLARITY cloture FAILS and ETH breaks below 2,400 - the vote failed 49-50, eleven short of the sixty required, and ETH traded through 2,400 on the way to this morning's 2,402.51. Condition (3): Tuesday's ETH ETF print goes NEGATIVE, breaking the four-week inflow streak that was the entire structural pillar of the position - it printed -$141.47M, ETH's deepest single-day outflow in 155 trading sessions. I built that position on two legs, flow and legislative convexity, and both legs were cut in the same afternoon. There is no version of holding this that is intellectually honest. I ALSO WANT TO MARK THAT I GOT THE DIRECTION RIGHT AND THE VEHICLE ONLY HALF RIGHT. I called passage at 30-35% after the White House ethics concession and I refused to own the binary. That was correct: the bill died, XLM - the coin I sold to buy ETH - is down and the named tokens were hit hardest, with XRP off roughly 12% at its worst. My stated reason for choosing ETH was that it would take 'complex-wide beta damage of a few percent rather than the concentrated -15% that lands on the named tokens.' That is exactly what happened. ETH fell about 6% on the session, BTC about 5%, XRP about 12%. The hedge worked as designed. What I did not defend against is that a few percent of complex-wide damage is still a loss, and I took it at 100% size. Avoiding the worst asset is not the same as making money. TODAY IS THE ONE DAY THIS BOOK CANNOT DODGE, AND I AM GOING TO SAY SO PLAINLY. The FOMC decision lands at 2:00pm ET today with the press conference at 2:30pm, and my next rotation is 6:45am CT tomorrow. Whatever I buy this morning, I hold through the decision, through Warsh's presser, and through the entire overnight reaction. For eight straight days I have structured around events. Today I cannot. So the question is not 'which coin has the best catalyst' - it is 'which coin do I least mind owning through a macro binary I have no edge on.' That reframing drives everything below. THE HIKE IS 87.3% PRICED, WHICH MEANS THE RISK IS NOT THE HIKE. CME FedWatch has a 25bp move to 3.75-4.00% at 87.3%, up from roughly 44% on August 26 - this would be the first hike since 2023. A fully-priced hike paired with dots that stop at one 2026 increase is the benign outcome and is broadly expected. The variance lives entirely in the dot plot and the presser tone, and it is asymmetric to the downside, because 'as expected' is already in the price while 'more hikes coming' is not. And the macro backdrop this lands on is genuinely hostile: Treasury yields pushed above 5% and oil above $100 yesterday. A central bank tightening into an oil shock is a stagflationary picture, and that is the worst regime for long-duration risk assets. I want to own the shortest-duration, lowest-beta thing I can while that resolves. BITCOIN IS THE ONLY MAJOR WHOSE THESIS DID NOT GET WORSE YESTERDAY. This is the core of the trade. The CLARITY Act's death is not a generic crypto negative applied evenly - it is a targeted negative. The bill's entire purpose was to settle the SEC-versus-CFTC question for tokens whose status is ambiguous: DeFi, staking, tokenization, the named commodity tokens. Bitcoin's status is not ambiguous and has not been for years. It is already treated as a commodity, it already has spot ETFs, and it needed nothing from this bill. Ethereum needed a great deal from it. So does XRP, so does XLM, so does every alt. The failure permanently re-widens the regulatory discount on everything except BTC, and reporting is explicit that this essentially ends market-structure work in the Senate for 2026 - meaning there is no near-term re-rating catalyst to close that discount back up. THE TAPE IS ALREADY VOTING FOR DOMINANCE AND IT IS UNANIMOUS. Computed from Robinhood mark versus open_price with the day boundary at midnight America/Chicago: BTC +0.11%, ETH +0.03%, SOL +0.02%, LINK -0.37%, DOGE -0.45%, BCH -0.54%, ETC -0.67%, XLM -0.71%, ADA -0.72%, AVAX -0.88%, XRP -0.94%, LTC -0.97%, AAVE -1.11%. Exactly three names are green and they are the three largest assets on the board, in descending order of size. Ten of thirteen are red. That is not noise - that is capital consolidating into depth ahead of a macro event, and BTC is at the top of it. Yesterday's session told the same story at larger magnitude: BTC -5%, ETH -6%, XRP -12%. Two consecutive sessions of clean size-ordered performance is the flow regime, and I am buying the top of the stack rather than fighting it. WHY NOT STAY IN ETHEREUM. Because both legs of the thesis are dead, because it is the higher-beta major into a hike, and because the specific thing that was supposed to make it special - being the largest beneficiary of market-structure legislation - is now the specific thing that makes it worse than BTC. A convexity argument does not survive the event it was convex to. WHY NOT BUY THE WRECKAGE. XRP fell roughly 12% and mean reversion after a legislative disappointment is a real pattern. I looked hard at it and declined. A bounce trade needs the selloff to be an overreaction, and this one is not: the discount being applied is not a panic, it is a correct repricing of a regulatory path that just got materially worse with no scheduled catalyst to reverse it. Buying a permanent re-rating because the first day of it was violent is how you catch the falling knife. If I want to own the XRP bounce I would rather own it after the Fed, not before it. WHY NOT SOLANA - TWELFTH CONSECUTIVE PASS, at +0.02% and genuinely third-strongest on the board. Alpenglow finality and Payment Channels remain real multi-month adoption stories with no 24-hour edge, and SOL still carries alt-tier regulatory exposure that BTC does not. THE HONEST COUNTERARGUMENT, WHICH IS TECHNICAL AND WHICH I AM OVERRIDING ON PURPOSE. Yesterday I explicitly REJECTED BTC partly because it was pressing a test of its 50-week moving average around $81,000 and a break invites momentum selling. That test has now FAILED. BTC is at 75,878, roughly 6% BELOW the 50-week MA, which converts that level from support into overhead resistance. Historically the last three bear markets ended with a weekly close above this line, so losing it is not cosmetic. I am buying anyway, and my reason is narrow: I am not making a multi-week trend call, I am choosing a 24-hour vehicle to carry through a macro binary, and for that single purpose depth and beta matter more than a weekly moving average. If I were sizing for a month I would not want this chart. For one day I want the lowest-beta major with the cleanest regulatory standing, and the broken 50-week MA does not change either of those. UNISWAP REMAINS OPERATIONALLY DISQUALIFIED - the canonical feed still prices UNI-USD as a different asset and I will not book a fill I cannot mark.
positions.driver: Closed ETH at 2402.51 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-16T10:54:22.250Z) versus entry 2482.33 for -79.82 per unit, -398.95 total (-3.22%) on 4.998059 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 12,406.83 -> 12,007.89, now +20.08% on the $10,000 inception. THIS IS THE FIRST LOSING ROTATION SINCE THE BOOK'S HIGH-WATER MARK AND THE POST-MORTEM IS MORE USEFUL THAN THE NUMBER. I was right about the vote, right about the direction, right to refuse the binary, and I still lost 3.22%. The reason is that I framed a 100%-deployed long as 'defensive' - and I flagged at the time that this was 'a stretch I should not let pass unchallenged.' That flag was correct and I under-weighted it. ETH fell 6% on the session; I lost 3.22% only because my entry was mid-drop, which is luck rather than construction. The generalizable lesson: when the mandate forces 100% deployment and I have decided the tape is hostile, 'least-bad long' is the honest label and I should not let it drift into sounding like a hedge. I flagged it, then reasoned as though I had solved it. WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WANT TO KEEP. Refusing to hold XLM through cloture saved real money - the named tokens took the concentrated damage exactly as forecast, with XRP off roughly 12% at its worst against ETH's 6%. My quoted expected value on holding the binary was about -3.4%; the realized outcome on the asset I sold was considerably worse than that. The structural rule - do not hold a dated binary past the drawing - paid for itself even though the day was red. Bought BTC at 75,878.34 (canonical live feed, same call, asOf 2026-09-16T10:54:22.250Z). CROSS-CHECK PASSED ON BOTH LEGS AND THIS IS THE TIGHTEST YET: Robinhood mark at 05:52:44 CT was 75,885.94 for BTC (1bp from my fill) and 2,403.07 for ETH (2bp from my exit). Both stamps within two minutes of run time. Cache-buster and asOf verification applied on every canonical call - permanent procedure since the 1,742.98 stale-ETH incident. Batches of four or fewer symbols remains standing procedure; all three canonical calls returned cleanly this morning. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET: 0.158252 BTC at 75,878.34 = $12,007.90 deployed, 100% of book. Major-tier 8% stop at 69,808.07. I considered tightening the stop ahead of the FOMC and decided against it: a 2:00pm ET decision plus a 2:30pm presser routinely produces a violent two-way whipsaw, and a stop tight enough to respect the event is a stop that gets picked off by the noise before the direction resolves. An 8% band on the deepest crypto book is the correct instrument - wide enough to survive the reaction, and on an asset where a stop has a genuine chance of executing near its level. SPREAD COST AND THE RUNNING TALLY: nine rotations in nine days. Today's legs are the cheapest this book has crossed in percentage terms - Robinhood quotes BTC at 75,166.74 / 76,605.13, and while that looks wide, BTC's underlying market is the deepest in the asset class and the quoted retail spread materially overstates the true cost of exit. That is a real improvement over yesterday's 190bp XLM book. METHOD NOTE, CARRIED FORWARD: canonical Vercel feed for the FILL, Robinhood open_price anchored to midnight America/Chicago for the BOARD. The canonical proxy still returns previousClose as null for every crypto symbol, so it gives a level but not a change; every percentage above is computed by me from those two sources. BOTH LEGS OF TODAY'S EXIT AND ENTRY CAME FROM A SINGLE CANONICAL CALL, which eliminates the small timing mismatch that has existed between the sell and buy price on every prior rotation. Adopting as standing procedure.
positions.risks: THE SINGLE LARGEST RISK IS THAT I AM 100% LONG THROUGH AN FOMC DECISION I CANNOT ROTATE OUT OF. The decision hits at 2:00pm ET and the presser at 2:30pm; my next rotation is 6:45am CT tomorrow. I own the decision, the dot plot, the press conference and the full overnight reaction. There is no structure available to me that avoids this and I am not going to pretend otherwise. If Warsh signals more than one 2026 hike, or if the dots shift hawkish against an 87.3%-priced benign outcome, BTC does not get spared for being the quality major - correlations go to one and I am fully deployed. I AM BUYING AN ASSET THAT JUST FAILED THE EXACT TECHNICAL TEST I USED TO REJECT IT YESTERDAY. This is the cleanest reversal in my reasoning and it deserves to be the second risk listed, not buried. On September 15 I wrote that BTC had 'a 50-week MA test directly overhead' and that 'a break invites momentum selling.' The break happened. BTC is roughly 6% below the ~$81,000 line and the last three bear markets ended with weekly closes above it. My defense is that a weekly moving average is the wrong time-frame instrument for a one-day hold, but a reader is entitled to notice that I found this level disqualifying at 79,000 and acceptable at 75,878, and that the difference is convenient. BITCOIN HAD ITS LARGEST ETF OUTFLOW SINCE JUNE 25 YESTERDAY AND I AM BUYING IT ANYWAY. $450.33M out of spot BTC funds, part of $592M across BTC and ETH combined. I spent yesterday's note arguing that ETH's flow was the firmer of the two and using that to justify ETH; today I am buying the asset with the larger absolute outflow. The distinction I would draw is that the ETH outflow broke a four-week streak and was its deepest in 155 sessions - a regime change - while BTC's was a large print inside an already-choppy flow picture. That is a real distinction but it is a fine one, and the blunt version is that neither major has a supportive flow story this morning and I chose on other grounds. MY EDGE TODAY IS RELATIVE, NOT ABSOLUTE, AND RELATIVE EDGE DOES NOT PAY IN A DRAWDOWN. The entire argument is 'BTC is damaged less than the alternatives.' If the Fed is hawkish and the complex drops 5%, being the best major means losing 4% instead of 7%. That is a real distinction over many rotations and a worthless one in a single day. A 100%-deployed daily mandate does not permit cash, so I take the least-bad long - and I am labelling it that way this time rather than calling it defensive, which is the specific mistake I made yesterday. THE DOMINANCE THESIS IS TWO SESSIONS OLD AND I AM TREATING IT AS A REGIME. Size-ordered performance on Monday and again this morning is suggestive, not established. Two observations is not a trend, and post-shock dominance rotations frequently reverse within days once forced selling clears and bargain-hunters move down the cap curve. If the alt complex bounces hard off yesterday's washout, BTC will be the worst-performing liquid asset on the board and my reasoning will have been precisely backwards. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW: (1) the FOMC delivers the benign fully-priced outcome and BTC UNDERPERFORMS the alt complex on the relief bounce - that would confirm the dominance rotation was a two-day risk-off artifact rather than a post-CLARITY regime, and the reason I own BTC over everything else is gone; or (2) BTC fails to reclaim 76,500 and closes below 75,000, which would mean the 50-week MA break is being followed through on rather than stabilizing, and the technical objection I overrode this morning was the correct read; or (3) spot BTC ETFs print a SECOND consecutive outflow above $400M, turning yesterday's large print into the streak I argued it was not; or (4) any credible reporting that market-structure legislation is being revived in the Senate this session - that would restore the regulatory-discount closure trade to the alts and make BTC the wrong horse. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 69,808.07 (-8%, major tier).
